response.markdown_report:
The proposed experiment is **suffix-augmented, multiple-negative training for the corrected NextItNet**. It targets broad relevance displacing specific recent matches and older interactions persisting despite coherent recent behavior. Improvement remains a hypothesis.

**Insights and directions.** Three observations guide the starting point: (1) causal dilated convolutions preserve order but do not explicitly identify obsolete interests; (2) Electronics’ negative lower-tail margin (−0.2595) and 12.27% sampled ranking-error rate motivate better discrimination; (3) mapped cosine scores near 0.5 provide little evidence of directional collapse, so an embedding-diversity penalty lacks current justification. These observations concern different mechanisms and should be tested separately.

Three literature insights suggest practical directions. NextItNet supplies the required causal backbone [1]. Sampled-softmax research motivates learning against several competing items, while warning that temperature affects gradient concentration [2]. TiCoSeRec motivates investigating changing preferences, although elapsed time does not establish obsolete intent [3]. CLA-Rec motivates behavioral/text alignment, but its results do not establish benefits from a randomly initialized text encoder here [4].

| Direction | Mechanism | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Context selection | Suffix augmentation | How much older context remains useful? |
| Discrimination | Multiple-negative softmax | Do training margins translate to HR@10? |
| Semantic sharing | Joint title encoder | Is corpus-only supervision sufficient? |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive (+) and limitation (−).

1. **Suffix-augmented multiple-negative softmax** [1–3]: **4/7/8/8/4**. Originality: + connects context restriction and discrimination, − familiar components. Potential: + inexpensive transferable experiment, − truncation may remove useful preferences. User: + targets stale context and broad matches, − cannot establish practical compatibility. Model: + trains against competing negatives, − sampled-margin gains may not transfer. Difficulty: + standard tensor operations, − sampling and predictor parity require care.
2. **Weak joint title alignment** [4]: **4/6/6/5/6**. Originality: + constrained adaptation, − established alignment concept. Potential: + shared-token transfer, − sparse text supervision. User: + finer item identity, − similarity cannot establish need. Model: + may distinguish sparse items, − may introduce semantic confusion. Difficulty: + small encoder, − vocabulary and serialization changes.
3. **Learned temporal convolution attenuation** [1,3]: **5/6/7/5/8**. Originality: + time-conditioned convolution taps, − temporal weighting is established. Potential: + models timing sensitivity, − gaps are ambiguous. User: + attenuates stale context, − persistent tastes may suffer. Model: + context-dependent separation, − no direct diagnostic evidence. Difficulty: + preserves backbone, − requires timestamp plumbing throughout training and inference.

**Selected experiment.** At 0% progress, prioritize candidate 1. Randomly retain a recent suffix during training and replace the baseline loss with moderate multiple-negative softmax. Compare baseline, suffix-only, softmax-only, and combined configurations separately; never combine their predictions. Select solely by fixed macro validation HR@10. Measure Electronics’ existing margin diagnostics and simulator preference for specific recent matches. Neither compatibility nor duplication is claimed solved.

idea.description: Train the corrected NextItNet with stochastic recent-suffix inputs and a moderate multiple-negative softmax objective. Keep one jointly trained network and one selected checkpoint per category. The proposal explicitly targets broad relevance outranking specific recent matches and stale interactions persisting despite coherent recent behavior; it also targets Electronics’ weak sampled positive-negative separation.
idea.motivation: Early research progress favors a small training change over additional convolution branches or timestamp-dependent architecture. Suffix augmentation tests whether excessive historical context contributes to the two user-facing failures, while multiple-negative softmax tests whether discrimination against several alternatives improves the observed lower-tail margins. These mechanisms are hypotheses, not established causes of the supplied diagnosis. Missing compatibility and purchase-need information limits what this method can resolve.
idea.implementation_notes: Use the supplied corrected baseline without inventing its architecture or optimizer settings. Preserve NextItNet, causal masking, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch and ModelView. For each training row, retain its full history with probability 0.5; otherwise sample a suffix length uniformly from 1 through its nonpadding length. Zero preceding sequence positions and mask their losses; preserve every retained position’s original next-item target. Keep left padding and prevent dropped context from entering any temporal layer. Retain the baseline explicit empty-history behavior. Initially use eight unique uniform negatives per valid position and temperature 1.0; exclude padding, the target and known training positives using training histories only. Do not consult validation or test interactions for negative filtering. Optimize ordinary sampled classification loss with no claim that it is an unbiased full-catalog softmax estimator. Keep raw model dot products at inference. The exact numerical configuration is a prespecified starting hypothesis, not a literature-derived optimum. Compare baseline, suffix-only, softmax-only and combined configurations only if their projected training, diagnostics and failed-run costs fit the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; declare any omitted contrasts. Each configuration contains four separately trained category models and is never fused with another configuration. Retain preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, baseline optimizer and validation schedule, single-GPU execution, all four category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Preserve the checkpoint rule and use the fixed macro validation HR@10 for configuration selection. Prediction uses full available history and the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1. Update the embedded predictor writer if any model configuration or checkpoint format changes; verify evaluation-mode score parity after reconstruction. Deploy exactly one checkpoint per category. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), with measured metrics and definitions and the B×L loader contract. Keep diagnostic sampling unchanged for comparability. Mark category/ratings/review breakdowns unavailable; the conflicting generic metadata examples do not authorize those fields. Report supplied user findings as qualitative evidence, and collect simulator rejection reasons only through supported host diagnostics. No validation improvement or diagnostic outcome is asserted before execution.
idea.pseudocode:
prespecify configurations and budget using the supplied baseline costs
for configuration in permitted_configurations:
    for category in the four required categories:
        initialize corrected NextItNet using seed 42
        for epoch in range(at_most_200):
            for batch in exactly_200_batches:
                sequence, positive, baseline_negative = family_sample_batch()
                if suffix_augmentation_enabled:
                    for each row:
                        keep full history with probability 0.5
                        otherwise retain a uniformly sampled nonempty recent suffix
                        zero earlier sequence entries and disable their target losses
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                if multiple_negative_loss_enabled:
                    negatives = sample_8_unique_uniform_items_per_valid_position(
                        excluding_padding_target_and_known_training_positives)
                    positive_score = model.predict_score(features, positive)
                    negative_scores = model.predict_score(features, negatives)
                    loss = mean_valid(-positive_score + logsumexp(
                        concatenate(positive_score, negative_scores)))
                else:
                    loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, baseline_negative)
                update the single model jointly
            apply unchanged host validation and checkpoint rule
        save one selected checkpoint and its configuration
        verify embedded-predictor score parity
select a configuration by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10
predict with full histories and final nonpadding features
load exactly one selected NextItNet checkpoint per category

originality.positive: Combines a controlled context intervention with discrimination training inside the required NextItNet family.
originality.negative: Suffix augmentation and multiple-negative classification are established techniques; this is a task-specific experimental combination.

future_potential.positive: The separate component controls can reveal whether context dependence or negative discrimination is the more useful direction.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may depend on the sampled candidate benchmark, and truncation can damage stable long-term preferences.

code_difficulty.positive: The backbone and inference computation remain intact; changes concentrate in batching and loss computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct target masking, efficient history exclusions, increased negative-scoring cost and save/reload consistency require verification.

related_work.title: Next Item Recommendation with Self-Attention? No: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network
contributions: Establishes NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutional approach to sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone retained by the proposed experiment.
limitations: Does not establish that suffix augmentation or the proposed loss improves this matched benchmark.
Causal ordering alone does not identify obsolete preferences or practical product compatibility.

related_work.title: Wu et al. (2024): sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: The supplied search summary reports that sampled softmax emphasizes high-scoring negatives.
Motivates testing multiple-negative training before adding explicit hard-negative mining.
limitations: Temperature and negative composition affect optimization.
The supplied evidence does not establish gains for the corrected NextItNet on these four categories.

related_work.title: TiCoSeRec (AAAI 2023)
contributions: Uses interval-aware augmentation to investigate irregular interaction timing and preference drift.
Motivates studying context usefulness as a separate research direction.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed order-based suffix augmentation.
Long gaps do not prove that an earlier interest has become irrelevant.

related_work.title: CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)
contributions: Contrastively aligns item-description embeddings with collaborative information.
Motivates an alternative experiment using jointly trained text features.
limitations: The supplied search evidence does not establish benefits for a corpus-only text encoder trained from scratch.
Text similarity does not establish compatibility, complementarity or purchase need.
